topics.label: Course introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the course instructors, format, and primary learning objectives on cancer etiology and carcinogen appraisal.

topics.label: Etiology of cancer: endogenous mutations, genetics, environment, and epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the fundamental origins of cancer by comparing intrinsic cellular errors and inherited predispositions with environmental exposures, supported by epidemiological and migrant data.

topics.label: Pathogens and infectious agents in oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how viral, bacterial, and parasitic infections drive cancer development, with a specific focus on Epstein-Barr virus and Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens, metabolic bioactivation, and DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyze how specific dietary, environmental, and chemical mutagens undergo xenobiotic bioactivation to form DNA adducts and mutations.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, chronic inflammation, and windows of tissue susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine non-mutagenic mechanisms that facilitate cancer growth, including inflammatory promoters, two-stage carcinogenesis models, and developmental stages of vulnerability.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying carcinogens and proving carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics present the investigative techniques used to assess carcinogenic potential, ranging from mutational signatures and biobanks to animal bioassays and the Ames test.
